storyboard.addedInformation: The wallet and coin name what buys the joy — dollars, not health.
storyboard.claim: A million dollars buys enormous joy at 30.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A coin — the million dollars that buys adventure and mobility at 30.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the healthspan-as-wallet argument: money converts best while young.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hospital bed shows why the money fails — the body, not the bank account.
storyboard.claim: The same million buys almost nothing at 85 with a bad hip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — no icon; an old patient slumped in a hospital bed, the body that cannot spend.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same money, opposite outcome: youth celebrated, age slumps.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the three resources as buckets the narrator then deals out across life stages.
storyboard.claim: Life is a balancing act between time, health, and money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three buckets — time, health, money — the triangle the hosts describe.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the 85-year-old's empty wallet to the system behind it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The clock makes the missing resource visible: midlife has money and health, not hours.
storyboard.claim: In middle age you have money and health but no time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock — the time consumed by career and children.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deals out the triangle's middle stage after naming its three buckets.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass marks this as the last stage — sand out, health out.
storyboard.claim: In old age you have money and time, but health is gone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass run out beside a slumped old saver with money and hours left.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The triangle's third stage, staged to visualize as promised.

storyboard.addedInformation: The key names the price paid — $25,000 saved over twenty years for this door.
storyboard.claim: You save $25,000 for the dream Tuscan villa pinned for decades.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The villa itself — the house from the vision board, key in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the abstract third stage to its concrete example.

storyboard.addedInformation: Sitting (not strolling Florence) shows the knees failing that the audio only describes.
storyboard.claim: Bad knees strand you on the porch instead of walking Florence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — no icon reads as knees; a traveler sitting out the trip on a porch above cobblestone streets.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The villa dream collapses into two weeks on the porch.

storyboard.addedInformation: Slumped shoulders say which wallet is empty — the health one, though cash is full.
storyboard.claim: Money and time mean nothing with the health wallet empty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a wallet icon would read as 'no money', the opposite of the claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the mechanism behind the ruined villa trip.

storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing at the trainer plan stages health spending as a deliberate purchase.
storyboard.claim: Trainers, sleep, food, sabbaticals are health spending, not luxury.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman mid-stride on a walk, heart strong: the trainer-sleep-food prescription in motion.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the empty wallet to how to fill it midlife.

storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the 'luxury cost' framing the narrator refuses.
storyboard.claim: These are not luxury costs but structural investments in the exchange rate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the struck-through phrase carries the rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the label the previous beat's spending is usually given.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins himself introduces the comparison the hosts then unpack.
storyboard.claim: Perkins illustrates biological versus chronological age with Ann and Betty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the author presenting his comparison, no drawable object.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From health investing to the comparison that proves it.

storyboard.addedInformation: Walking fit at 50 shows the diet-and-fitness priority in her body.
storyboard.claim: Ann, 50, prioritized health, diet, and fitness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Ann herself mid-stride, the fit 50-year-old.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First half of the comparison: the woman who invested.

storyboard.addedInformation: Celebrating ten years younger makes the cellular age visible on her face.
storyboard.claim: Ann's biological age is 40.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a clock would read as schedule time, not cellular age.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payoff of Ann's priority: a decade younger inside.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slump and sedentary body stage the neglect the narration lists.
storyboard.claim: Betty neglected her health with a sedentary job and poor diet.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a food icon would read as dining, missing the neglect.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second half of the comparison: the woman who did not invest.

storyboard.addedInformation: The target marks the peak net-worth date each woman aims at differently.
storyboard.claim: Biologically 65, Betty peaks earlier; Ann's peak date comes later.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ann vibrant beside a strong heart, Betty tired: healthspan sets each peak date.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The comparison resolves into different drawdown dates.

storyboard.addedInformation: Celebration stages what the decade buys — years of convertible experiences.
storyboard.claim: Ann's larger healthspan wallet buys an extra decade of experiences.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ann vibrant and striding, heart strong: the larger healthspan wallet in motion.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ann's later peak restated as time bought, not money kept.

storyboard.addedInformation: Clutching the coin stages the seductive question — can the pile buy it back?
storyboard.claim: Can I hoard wealth, grind, and buy health back later?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A coin clutched while thinking — the hoarded pile offered against aging.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pushback against the invest-early moral: why not just pay later?

storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing at his own knees names what the $5,000 actually protects.
storyboard.claim: $5,000 on a trainer at 50 buys more life quality per dollar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Coins stacked against a trainer whistle and a knee brace: five thousand buying future mobility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the buy-it-later question with the asymmetry.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hospital bed stages the expensive, diminished recovery cash actually buys.
storyboard.claim: Twice the savings at 70 buys a titanium joint and a hard recovery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass running out beside the pricey surgery: decay no cash reverses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The other side of the asymmetry: what late money buys.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shield makes prevention literal — protection bought in your 40s.
storyboard.claim: Prevention in your 40s beats ten pounds of cure later.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield — protection bought early for the biological wallet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The asymmetry compressed into the proverb.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host turn signals the summation — commentary, not story.
storyboard.claim: All of temporal economics builds to one final crescendo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — pure show transition; the host gathers the threads.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from the health proof to the book's closing mandate.

storyboard.addedInformation: The author's pointed finger delivers his own mandate, not the hosts'.
storyboard.claim: Memory dividends, buckets, drawdown, healthspan compress into: spend with audacity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the mandate is a command, and Perkins gives it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The crescendo lands as a single imperative.

storyboard.addedInformation: Reaching past the money stages fulfillment as the thing to grab.
storyboard.claim: Maximize lifetime fulfillment points, not net worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a trophy would read as status, the opposite of the reframe.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mandate's goal named: points, not dollars.

storyboard.addedInformation: The worried calculation on his face is the personal interest rate at work.
storyboard.claim: The older you get, the more delaying an experience must pay you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — survival odds dropping yearly live in the worried weighing, not an icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Prices the fulfillment goal against shrinking survival odds.

storyboard.addedInformation: Host commentary marks the investing-world contrast before the finance examples.
storyboard.claim: This is a fascinating shift from traditional investing thought.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — banter bridge; the host reacts before the return-on-equity beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A breath between the interest-rate idea and its finance foil.

storyboard.addedInformation: The exchange icon plus the clutched coin stage the yield-obsession being described.
storyboard.claim: Finance trains obsession over yields and cap rates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman fixated on a target of yields and rates: return chased, life unmeasured.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The old lens: returns on money, about to be replaced.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone shows the booking page; the kitchen island anchors the late-night scene.
storyboard.claim: Stop calculating return on equity; calculate return on experience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the man at his kitchen island staring at the New Zealand booking page.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The replacement lens, staged at the island where the choice happens.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hovering finger over the phone is the $10k-versus-index-fund sweat.
storyboard.claim: Ten grand for New Zealand or into the S&P 500?
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a coin would pick a side; the hovering indecision is the beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The new lens tested on one sweating finger.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins's jabbing finger is the scream — bet while youth favors you.
storyboard.claim: Buy the ticket; bet on experience while youth and health favor you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the command lands through the author's pointed insistence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hovering resolves: Perkins shouts the answer.

storyboard.addedInformation: The notes in hand are the cap-rate spreadsheets Paulie tortures himself with.
storyboard.claim: Paulie agonizes over buying a Central American vacation property.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The property itself — the house under analysis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The book's proof story for buying the ticket.

storyboard.addedInformation: Poring over the notes stages analysis paralysis no finance icon could.
storyboard.claim: Paulie paralyzes himself over a measly 3% rental yield.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the man buried in his own yield math.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The property narrows to the 3% he cannot stop analyzing.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows paralysis winning — the return studied, the life unlived.
storyboard.claim: The 3% obsession paralyzes him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — paralysis is a body state, staged slumped over the numbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Obsession hardens into paralysis.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins jabbing at the smaller man stages the grab the narration describes.
storyboard.claim: Perkins grabs him: forget the money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a coin would stage the money plainly, defying the rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Perkins interrupts the paralysis with both hands.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shoreline plus the family mark the beach memories the property exists for.
storyboard.claim: The property buys family beach memories before the kids grow up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A family on the beach — the memories Perkins demands he count.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What to count instead of the 3%: the beach years.

storyboard.addedInformation: The cascade shows dividends compounding — one trip toppling into decades of stories.
storyboard.claim: 3% cash means nothing beside 300% in memory dividends.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The children at the center of the asset: the property paying its 300 percent in family memory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The 3% versus 300% verdict, visualized as compounding.

storyboard.addedInformation: The worried second-guess after booking stages the leap-of-faith fear.
storyboard.claim: I booked New Zealand — but what if the trip is a disaster?
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — the fear is hypothetical; staging plain disaster would endorse it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The leap taken, the fear arrives after.

storyboard.addedInformation: The storm plus the broken-ankle slump stage the worst case the host fears.
storyboard.claim: Rain for 28 days, a broken ankle, miserable kids, regretted cash.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The imagined disaster reel: storm clouds over the planned New Zealand trip, a fear voiced not a forecast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The disaster spelled out: weather, injury, misery.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host's level tone pulls back from the disaster to the macro frame.
storyboard.claim: The fear of a bad investment is real — but pull back to a lifetime.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — commentary beat; the host reframes before answering.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the worst case to naming the fear behind it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The cemetery hill makes the grave literal — unspent money beside an unspent life.
storyboard.claim: The only irredeemable regret is the grave with unspent money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave — the arrival point where unspent dollars accuse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The macro answer: one regret outweighs every bad trip.

storyboard.addedInformation: Raising a cup at the party stages where worst trips end up — retold laughing.
storyboard.claim: The worst trips become the funniest dinner-party stories.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a food icon would read as dining, but the beat is about storytelling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Even the disaster beat is redeemed as future comedy.
